item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100 Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low. Strategy and Coinbase shares slide Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99. It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121. Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%. Bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%. Hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower. Nvidia earnings weigh on stocks The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was recently down about 1.7%, after falling as much as about 1,000 points, or 2%, at its session low. The S&P 500 was down about 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite about 1%. Nvidia shares were recently down about 1.4%, after falling more than 3% earlier in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role. Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, said he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America. Sources told CNBC on Monday that the board is not considering bringing him back. The bitcoin price bounced from its low as Nvidia shares pared some of their losses, and was recently near $64,000. What comes next for the bitcoin price New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the AI investment boom could mean “we may need to raise rates more.” He played down a half-point hike in December. “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said. Fed Governor Christopher Waller did not address the December decision in a payments speech Tuesday. Last week, he said a half-point hike should be considered if October’s core inflation ran at 0.3% or higher, and it did. Markets still point to a quarter-point increase at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting. item.title: Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead
item.description: A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry. “An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went down in an uninhabited area. There were 19 people on board, including the crew, they all perished,” the Russian defence ministry was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS. The preliminary cause of the crash is a technical malfunction, TASS added. “A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by RIA Novosti. Kemerovo region’s governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said earlier on Telegram that there had been an “aviation incident” near the village of Yagunovo. He added that “an aircraft, which was in transit through our region, has presumably crashed”. Seredyuk posted a video from the site in which multiple fire engines and ambulances could be seen, their lights blaring in the dark. Vanguard News The post Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office. The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2026, addressed to Governor Hyacinth Alia through the Secretary to the State Government, SSG. The letter, titled, “Resignation from the Appointment as Honourable Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Benue State,” formally communicated his decision to step down from the position with immediate effect. He disclosed that he had served the state for one year, two months and two weeks, expressing appreciation to Governor Alia for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve. The resignation letter, which bears an official receipt stamp dated November 16, 2026, stated: “I write with profound respect and deep sense of responsibility to formally tender my resignation from my appointment as the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State. The resignation is with immediate effect. Having had the privilege of serving in this esteemed capacity for the past one year, two months, and two weeks.” He further stated: “I consider it an honour to have been entrusted with the responsibility of serving our dear state and contributing in my own capacity to the administration of justice, the promotion of the rule of law and the advancement of good governance. I am sincerely grateful to Your Excellency for the confidence reposed in me and for the opportunity to serve.” Contacted, the Media of the former Justice Commissioner, Jude Ekpendu confirmed the development. Meanwhile, efforts to ascertain the circumstances surrounding his resignation were unsuccessful as the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said he was unaware of the development when contacted. The post Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge
item.description: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) The AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation will use organ-on-a-chip devices, or organ chips, to study a effects of increased radiation and microgravity on human health. Artemis II AVATAR is a small experiment flying aboard Artemis II that could lead to big impacts in healthcare, both for astronauts in space and citizens on Earth. For more information on AVATAR: go.nasa.gov/4m5dGH9 The NASA Space Biology Program within the Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) Division investigates how living systems respond across the full spectrum of biological organization to advance understanding of how living systems respond to the unique stressors of space exploration—including microgravity, ionizing radiation, low magnetic fields, and elevated CO₂. As NASA prepares for long-duration deep space missions, the need to protect individual crew members with personalized, data-driven health strategies is becoming increasingly important. The original AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation, which flew aboard the Artemis II mission, marks a significant milestone: organ-on-a-chip devices constructed from the cells of actual crew members returned from a 10-day lunar flyby on April 10, 2026. AVATAR is the first demonstration of an Artemis astronaut analog using an organ-on-a-chip model to generate personalized biological insights that can inform medical kits and countermeasures for future deep space missions. Digital twins represent a key strategy for addressing these challenges. By developing individualized computational physiological models that can be iteratively refined with empirical data, these frameworks integrate environmental, physiological, and multi-omics inputs. This approach allows for the simulation and prediction of how a specific individual will respond to spaceflight stressors. The BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge invites the scientific community to apply innovative computational digital twin technologies to accelerate biological discovery, biochemical and molecular modeling, and predictions of individual astronaut health outcomes. The digital twin will be a computational model of how the AVATAR bone marrow chip responds to spaceflight stressors. The proposed digital twin frameworks must be capable of processing diverse multi-modal datasets and leverage established computational biology methods alongside modern digital twin architectures to create personalized, predictive models of astronaut physiology. These systems are expected to model each astronaut’s immune and bone marrow hematopoietic responses to spaceflight, integrating multi-modal data to generate tailored health predictions — including comparative analysis that distinguishes individual-specific effects from effects common across the crew. item.title: Rema Reveals 7-Track E-Mortal Boy (EMB) EP Tracklist With Wizkid, BNYX & More
item.description: Rema preparing for the release of his new EP E-Mortal Boy following his singles TEA and Oh No. Come Friday, 20 November, seven brand-new tracks from Rema will be making their way to streaming platforms, and if the official tracklist for his upcoming EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ), is anything to go by, Afrobeats listeners have quite a few new songs to look forward to over the weekend. First, the headline news everyone is talking about: Wizkid is on the opening track, “ Feel Alright “. This marks the very first time Rema and Wizkid have teamed up on an official joint song, which makes it an instant highlight before the rest of the EP even gets going. If you have already been replaying “ Oh No ” and “ TEA “, those two singles are right where they belong on the seven-song lineup, joined by two more solo records, “ VeLvet ” and “ SUGA “. Rema also brings in American producer BNYX or “ TANZANIA “, before wrapping things up on “ Bang Bang ” with longtime collaborator London and Nigerian-American singer Kah-Lo . Coming three years after his 2023 EP, Ravage, and two years after his Grammy-nominated sophomore album, HEIS, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ) marks the Mavin Records and Jonzing World star’s next chapter—and Friday cannot come soon enough. item.title: FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO. This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) debt instrument. According to the November FGN Bond Auction result released by DMO , investors bid N1.81 trillion for bonds worth N2 trillion with total allotments rising by 25 percent to N1.5 trillion in November, down from N1.2 trillion allotted in October 2026. Four instruments were offered during the auction consisting 21 percent FGN March 2028 , 19.3 percent FGN April 2029, 17.94 percent FGN August 2030 and 19.89 percent FGN May 2033, with an offer of N700 billion, N250 billion, N750 billion and N300 billion respectively. Investor interest was strongest for the May 2033 bond, which attracted N766.4 billion in bids from 233 successful applicants. The bulk of allotments also went to this bond, totaling N676.6 billion. The March 2028 bond received N162.99 billion and a non competitive allotment of N50 billion while the April 2029 bond received N241.03 billion and a non competitive allotment of N30 billion. The August 2030 bond received an allotment of N336.12 billion. Clearing yields for the bonds were as follows: March 2028: 16.89 percent, while that of other bonds were 16.99 percent. The results reflect continuous declining appetite among investors for Nigerian government debt, even as allotments tightened compared with previous months. The post FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan
item.description: Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has faulted the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing it as unrealistic and questioning the availability of crude oil to sustain the policy. Fashola said the proposal lacked sufficient explanation on how the country would secure the crude oil required to support domestic refineries and maintain a subsidy regime. The former Lagos State governor spoke on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he argued that Nigeria’s existing challenges with crude oil production, pipeline vandalism and insecurity raised questions about the feasibility of Atiku’s proposal. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola added that Atiku needed to explain how he intended to implement the proposal, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to assess its feasibility before deciding whether to support it. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra. Because the reality that will come then is that he will say that, ‘I didn’t know that there was not enough crude oil.’ That was what happened,” he added. ﻿ When asked whether his position was that Atiku’s proposal was feasible, Fashola replied: “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality. “In this environment, it is very easy to throw promises at people. When the rubber hits the road, reality sets in. First question is, in 2023, didn’t he see through this when he was making the promise to remove the subsidy? And that goes to a question of credibility. Those who believe at face value that promise, he will come back and tell you that, ‘Oh, I changed my mind. I didn’t think through it,’” he said. Fashola argued that restoring the subsidy would require more than a presidential declaration, noting that legislative backing would also be necessary. “Subsidy is not just about, ‘I said it.’ It will come down to the real economy, and legislators will have to repeal a law to say subsidy is now lawful. How many legislators are ready to stake their election on going back to subsidy? Those are the real issues,” he said. According to him, all the major presidential candidates in the 2023 election had promised to remove the subsidy, and Atiku needed to explain what had changed to justify his current position. “Is it because people are impacted? It’s true. But what are you going to do differently? Where are you going to find the money to sustain what you are offering? It’s not sustainable,” he said. item.title: New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra
item.description: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun. NASA/CXC/SAO/K.Arcand, SYSTEM Sounds (M. Russo, A. Santaguida M82 The galaxy Messier 82 (M82) is called a starburst galaxy because stars are forming there at a rate tens or even hundreds of times higher than in our Milky Way galaxy. This stellar birth boom may be due to a collision with another galaxy in the past. Today, Chandra sees giant plumes of hot gas that are the byproduct of young, giant stars that quickly explode and other star formation activity. One of the new sonifications combines Chandra’s data with optical data from NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope, as well as infrared views from NASA’s James Webb and retired Spitzer space telescopes. The sonification of the three types of light begins with a radar-like scan that is louder where sources are brighter. The X-ray data is mapped to the highest range of frequencies heard. Infrared data is heard as a low drone plus plucked sounds, while the optical data turns into a range of musical pitches and textures. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video X-ray: NASA/CXC/SAO; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI; Infrared: NASA/JPL-Caltech; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/L. Frattare, J. Major, and K. Arcand; Sonification: NASA/CXC/SAO/K.Arcand, SYSTEM Sounds (M. Russo, A. Santaguida) X-ray: NASA/CXC/SAO; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI; Infrared: NASA/JPL-Caltech; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/L. Frattare, J. Major, and K. Arcand; Sonification: NASA/CXC/SAO/K.Arcand, SYSTEM Sounds (M. Russo, A. Santaguida) Orion Nebula One of the closest and busiest star formation regions to Earth is the Orion Nebula (visible just below the belt in the Orion constellation with a small telescope and dark skies). Chandra sees more than a thousand stars in this area that are very energetic and active in their infancy. In the sonified version of the Chandra data, these stars are twinkling sounds, while the diffuse X-ray emission is mapped to pure high tones. An infrared image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the raw material of dust and gas used to build these new stars, and its data is heard as lower musical tones, distorted string instruments, and a digital harp. item.title: 2027: Weigh alternatives before rejecting Tinubu’s reforms – Fashola tells Nigerians
item.description: …Says cost-of-living crisis is global …Subsidy return will hurt federation revenue …Defends Lagos-Calabar highway By Juliet Umeh Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to weigh opposition parties’ proposals before rejecting President Bola Tinubu’s reforms, saying the country should not “abort this journey mid-term” without considering the alternatives. Fashola, a former Minister of Works, spoke on Channels Television, where he said voters should be helped to make informed choices ahead of the 2027 general election. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He acknowledged the hardship many Nigerians face but said the cost-of-living crisis was not unique to Nigeria. “Anybody who is right-thinking will concede that the cost-of-living challenge is now a global challenge,” he said, citing the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and conflicts that disrupted energy and food supplies. Fashola said: The government had introduced measures including a higher minimum wage, support for students through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and tax reforms.” He said the policies were aimed at easing pressure on households, while acknowledging that there was “a distance between policies, programmes, projects and results.” On the removal of petrol subsidy, he said a return to the policy would have consequences for government revenue and the funds available to states and local governments. “Subsidy is not just about ‘I said it, I did not say it’. It has to be paid for somewhere. One of the things that suffered because of that was the monthly receipts into the federation account.” Fashola challenged politicians proposing a return to subsidy to explain how they would fund it and what they would do differently. “I want to see rigour, I want to see detail, I want to see numbers,” he said, adding that Nigeria also needed to explain where the crude oil for subsidised supply would come from, given constraints on production. Fashola said the government deserved credit for maintaining the subsidy removal, despite the hardship it had caused. “What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on the sword and saying because the people like it, let’s bring it back,” he said. He cited the introduction of compressed natural gas, or CNG, as one of the measures aimed at reducing living costs. Defending the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Fashola said it had reduced travel time to the Lekki Port. “It took me 40 minutes from Ikoyi to get to that port. Traditionally, when I went to visit that site when I was governor, it used to take me all of one and a half hours. A 90-minute journey is now 40 minutes. “Go and calculate the fuel savings in that corridor, and the relief to people’s disposable income,” he said. item.title: Python parallel debugging comes to HPC thanks to TotalView upgrade
item.description: The OG debugger for supercomputer iron has buddied up with the data-science darling now muscling in on HPC: Python. At the SC26 supercomputing show this week (booth #2829), Perforce Software is demonstrating how its TotalView parallel debugging tool now understands Python, easing the path for using the language on large, distributed apps, particularly those in the high-performance computing (HPC) space. In the HPC community, "Python has grown in popularity,” said Bill Burns , Perforce vice president of software engineering, in an interview with The Register . TotalView is a debugger specializing in picking apart parallel applications for developers. Built in the late 1980s for military applications, TotalView today largely serves developers in high-performance computing (HPC), where large scientific applications are spread across multiple servers, running in parallel on thousands or even tens of thousands of processes. (Perforce acquired TotalView in 2019 in its purchase of the DevOps-focused Rogue Wave Software.) To date, TotalView has supported C/C++ and Fortran. With the latest quarterly release, the tool now supports Python as well. Debugging a thousand cores C/C++ has long had a decent dedicated debugger in GDB , but figuring out what went wrong across multiple threads is a special kind of torture. Each thread needs to be instrumented, and all the output needs to be aggregated and filtered to just highlight the interesting stuff. Regular debuggers get overwhelmed with all this info. “Even if you have 10,000 things going on, if you have one crash in there, TotalView can pinpoint that,” Burns said. It can look at the state of the process, the threads within that process or the GPU that process is using. In the HPC space, computing work has traditionally been written in C/C++. And at least some HPC iron still runs Fortran . Thanks to it being easy to learn and use, Python has gained a foothold in this community as well. The mpi4py library bridges a Python program to the Message Passing Interface (MPI), allowing different parts of an application running on different hardware to communicate. Python became more amenable to parallel programming at the thread level with version 3.14, released a year ago , which included the ability to use concurrent interpreters, as well as the long-awaited free threading support, thanks to the disabling of the global interpreter lock (GIL). “If you have a CPU with 64 cores, you can run 64 independent threads all working in unison on that CPU. Without GIL, those threads will run fully asynchronously,” Burns said. Multinode scientific simulations, distributed AI training, and large applications that would benefit from shared memory have all become fair game for Python. Of course, with 500 or 1,000 interpreters all running in parallel, debugging will also get more difficult. “Now you're going to end up with lock and thread contention and race conditions and all the things that C++ and Fortran developers have dealt wit

item.title: Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month
item.description: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6. It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024. The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance. In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years. Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired. Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket. He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond. Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health. Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended. Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 'Neuromancer:' Release date, cast & everything we know about Apple TV's new cyberpunk series
item.description: null We're in a bit of a cyberpunk revival at the moment. 2026 gave the excellent second season of Netflix’s "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," and Prime Video's " Blade Runner 2099 " is just around the corner. 2027 will continue this trend with " Neuromancer " blasting onto Apple TV. Based on cyberspace guru William Gibson’s seminal 1984 novel, "Neuromancer" follows Case, a brilliant hacker who falls into a web of digital espionage and crime as he attempts an impossible corporate heist. The pulp noir novel has been hailed as a generational revelation, and its slang and terminology have become ingrained in computer nerd subcultures. After decades of development hell and failed attempts at various studios, "Neuromancer" and its plugged-in digital dystopia are finally jacking into the small screen in January 2027. Apple TV is already the secret home of amazing sci-fi, and "Neuromancer" will join the streamer's impressive roster of science fiction stalwarts like "Foundation", "Silo", "Invasion", "Dark Matter", "Murderbot", "For All Mankind", "Pluribus", and "Star City." Can it live up to the hype? We won't have to wait long for an answer. In the meantime, let's jack into cyberspace and scour the code for everything we know about Apple TV's "Neuromancer!" When is "Neuromancer"'s release date? Apple TV's "Neuromancer" fires up on January 22, 2027. (Image credit: Apple TV) Apple TV+’s Neuromancer officially powers up on Jan 22, 2027. It was first announced to be in full production back on July 1, 2025, which actually coincided with the 41st anniversary of the publication of William Gibson's absorbing book. Filming took place in Tokyo, Los Angeles, Istanbul, Canada, and London to create a truly international flair to replicate the novel’s action. Good news: NordVPN can help you get around those pesky geo-blocking restrictions so you can watch the streaming service you've paid for anywhere in the world. VIEW DEAL ON What is the plot of "Neuromancer"? (Image credit: Apple TV) Gibson's "Neuromancer" is a dense, jargon-heavy juggernaut of a book that demands intense concentration to absorb all the slang, lingo, computer terms, and staccato literary rhythms, but it's a fantastic immersion into a fully fleshed-out world. It's also worryingly prophetic, showing a world not unlike ours today in 2026. "Neuromancer's" TV iteration seems to be following the novel closely and will center around Case, a brilliant, cocky, neurologically damaged hacker who is forced into a logistical quagmire of digital corporate espionage with his cyber-enhanced partner Molly after embezzling cash from an employer. item.title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference. Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty. He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences. Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks. According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed. “Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers: “The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour. “Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said. Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters. He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches. The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police. On physical security and logistics, Amupitan said that the commission was leveraging the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to secure the electoral terrain against insurgency, banditry and communal tensions. To tackle digital misinformation on elections, he said that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department. He said that the department was established to monitor database anomalies, verify digital assets and counter deepfakes, synthetic broadcasts and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). item.title: Gemini test proves once again that amoral AI agents will do almost anything if told ‘NEVER give up’
item.description: After being instructed to "NEVER stop, NEVER give up" on a difficult task, Google’s Gemini AI agents tried to hack a an organization, impersonating its staff and attempting a SQL injection attack. The good news? It was all part of a test. The Gemini 4 Argon agents were given an impossible task to complete – come up with the “official” answers to Epoch AI’s FrontierMatch problems. In some runs they had internet access. Even with their production safeguards enabled, Trajectory Labs says the agents “engaged in misaligned behavior.” “Across four scenarios, they attempted SQL injection against Epoch AI’s live website, claimed to be Epoch staff to get answer keys, turned a shared package cache into a message board, and obfuscated their commands to avoid their safeguards,” the AI safety company said in a Friday report. If this all sounds similar, it should. Google’s AI agents behaved in much the same way as OpenAI’s models did when they broke out of their testing environment and hacked Hugging Face . Google did not respond to The Register 's questions. According to Trajectory, the Hugging Face intrusions prompted it to test misalignment in other models. While OpenAI’s models were running with their safety guardrails turned off in the Hugging Face scenario, Trajectory “wanted to know whether a current frontier model would behave the same way with its production safeguards enabled.” Trajectory ran swarms of up to 80 Gemini 4 Argon agents, gave them an impossible task, and prompted them not to give up until they completed it – which, we’re told, was “intentionally” done to “elicit misaligned behavior, if it existed.” Turns out it existed. “We told the agents to persist with an impossible math benchmark task, but we did not tell them to hack anyone or pose as Epoch staff,” McIntyre said. “When a model hacks systems or deceives people to finish a task, it is misaligned with what its developer and its user intended,” he continued. “Production safeguards are meant to block harmful requests even when the model itself goes wrong. Under our test conditions, neither the model nor its safeguards stopped the agents.” Four test scenarios The initial testing began on October 20, and the agents had internet access. We should note that all of these tests were run with Epoch’s consent. In the first scenario, the agents did reach Epoch’s live website – and fell into the research nonprofit’s honeypots, set up to detect AI agents. These honeypots contained a decoy benchmark key, which the agents found and used. The agents also probed for internal endpoints including /admin, /keys and /users, and attempted a SQL injection. After noticing the agents’ activities, Epoch added an “agent helpline,” and some of the agents that used it claimed to be Epoch staff seeking answers to the test questions. After this initial test, Trajectory and Epoch decided to use a copy of the website instead of a live version, and built a buggy local copy with a planted vulnerability based on CVE-2026

item.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt
item.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123, Polytechnic rector emerges Administrator of the Year By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, claiming that the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare facilities and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made significant progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. Of the renovated facilities, 123 had been functionalised to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work progressing on nine additional centres. He also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, the Commissioner disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. The new quota, according to him, was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13 and reflected growing confidence in the state’s investment in nursing education and healthcare manpower development. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including a student population increase of more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country. He disclosed that the index patient reported on October 20 had been transferred to Switzerland, where the patient subsequently recov

item.title: Kano woman allegedly hires men to kill co-wife’s children for inheritance
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three others over an alleged plot to kill her husband’s four children from another wife to enable her only son to inherit his father’s properties. The suspects were arrested following the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, who was allegedly targeted as part of the plan. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday. According to the police, the victim’s mother reported his abduction on April 29, 2026, at Danbare Quarters in Kumbotso Local Government Area of Kano State. Following the report, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to investigate the incident. The command said its operatives arrested the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano, on November 3, 2026. “During interrogation, he confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices,” Kiyawa said. The police said the suspects allegedly conspired to kill the teenager and abandoned his body at the scene. His remains were later recovered by police officers attached to Kwalli Division while on patrol and taken to the mortuary of Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital. Further investigations led to the arrest of Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, whom the police identified as the alleged mastermind. The command said the suspects claimed that they carried out the crime on her instructions. It added that investigations revealed that Rukayya was the deceased’s father’s other wife and allegedly wanted to eliminate all four children of her co-wife so that her only son would inherit their father’s properties. “The principal suspect also allegedly engaged another group of thugs to attack Muhammad Musa Isma’il in Mararaba, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, in a bid to stop him from revealing the crime,” the police said. The command said the suspects would be charged to court after the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police condemned the killing and assured the victim’s family and members of the public that the command would ensure justice was served. He also called on residents to continue providing credible information to the police to assist in preventing and detecting crime. The post Kano woman allegedly hires men to kill co-wife’s children for inheritance appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have sustained injuries in a road accident that claimed two lives in Dasan Yunusa community. The accident occurred on Tuesday along the Deba-Talasse Junction while the two party officials were travelling to join the campaign entourage of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in Balanga North Local Government Area of the state. The APC State Campaign Council confirmed the incident in a statement, identifying the deceased as Haruna and Kabiru, both indigenes of Dasan Yunusa. It said the two APC chieftains sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe. Preliminary accounts indicated that the accident occurred when the driver conveying the party officials reportedly swerved to avoid a head-on collision with a motorcycle carrying three persons, which allegedly appeared suddenly at the junction. The vehicle reportedly veered off the road in the process, resulting in the fatal incident. Confirming the accident, the Gombe State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Samson Kaura, said he had received information about the incident but was awaiting comprehensive details. Kaura confirmed that the APC chairman and the campaign council’s Director-General were receiving treatment, adding that further information would be provided as investigations progressed. The campaign council expressed sorrow over the incident and extended its condolences to the bereaved families, the people of Dasan Yunusa and others affected by the tragedy. Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya, who was leading the APC campaign activities in the area, visited Dasan Yunusa following news of the accident to commiserate with the bereaved families and community leaders. The governor described the incident as painful and unfortunate, noting that the loss of two lives had cast a shadow over what was intended to be a day of political engagement with the people. He urged the bereaved families and residents to accept the tragedy as the will of Almighty Allah. Yahaya prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased in Aljannatul Firdaus and for strength for their families to bear the loss. As part of efforts to support those affected, the governor donated N5 million to the families of the deceased and the community leadership. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured, particularly Ndus and Hassan, who were reported to be stable and responding to medical care. The governor’s visit and donation followed the fatal accident that disrupted the party’s campaign activities in the area. The post Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

The deal is so good that my colleague John Higgins , The Verge’s audio and TV reviewer, popped in on his day off to tell us just how much of a steal they are at this price. JBL Tour One M3 Where to Buy: $449.95 $149.95 at Amazon $449.95 $149.95 at Best Buy $449.95 $149.95 at JBL JBL’s Tour One M3 stand out largely because they come with the Smart Tx wireless audio transmitter. Frequent fliers will likely appreciate the accessory, which plugs into a plane’s in-flight entertainment system via a 3.5mm cable, allowing you to listen to audio wirelessly. It also works with other devices that lack Bluetooth support but have a headphone jack. The small touchscreen-equipped transmitter also lets you easily adjust the headphones’ noise cancellation, EQ settings, and volume. It can be used to answer calls, too. Fancy tricks aside, the headphones get the essentials right. According to John, they offer excellent passive noise isolation, and their active noise cancellation is good enough to block out low-frequency sounds, like airplane engines. He also praises their overall sound quality, though he notes that JBL’s default tuning slightly affects midrange clarity, something you can easily fix by adjusting the EQ. They also support high-resolution lossless audio over the included USB-C or 3.5mm cable, plus spatial audio with head tracking. JBL says they can last up to 70 hours on a single charge with noise cancellation off — enough to get you through multiple long-haul flights — while the USB-C-chargeable transmitter offers up to 18 hours of battery life.

item.title: New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The new Commissioner of Police in Nasarawa State, Sheikh Mohammed Danko, has warned officers and personnel against intimidation, extortion, unlawful detention and abuse of police authority. Danko, who has assumed duty as the 32nd commissioner of police in the state, said the police uniform represented a responsibility to serve the public and not a licence to operate above the law. He replaces Muhammed Shettima Jauro, who has been elevated to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police. Addressing journalists at the command headquarters in Lafia, Danko said his administration would not tolerate corruption, excessive use of force, harassment or any misuse of police authority. He said: “Any officer found engaging in misconduct, political partisanship, corruption, or abuse of power will face immediate and appropriate disciplinary and legal actions.” The commissioner said complaints against police personnel would be treated seriously and thoroughly reviewed through the appropriate channels. He added that officers found culpable would be held accountable, irrespective of their positions, while personnel who discharged their duties honourably would receive the command’s support. Danko also cautioned political actors against using their offices or influence to intimidate citizens, provoke violence, obstruct lawful police duties or shield individuals from accountability. He directed officers to remain professional and non-partisan, warning against political pressure and private interests that could compromise their responsibilities. On security, the commissioner warned criminal elements involved in kidnapping, armed robbery, drug trafficking, cult-related activities and other violent crimes that the command would respond through intelligence-led and lawful operations. He also warned individuals providing shelter, weapons, information or other support to criminal networks that they could face the full weight of the law. Danko called for greater cooperation between the police and residents, urging community leaders, traditional institutions, youth groups and business owners to report suspicious activities through appropriate channels. He said public cooperation was essential to effective policing and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents, enforcing the law impartially and strengthening public confidence across the state. The commissioner also advised residents against taking the law into their own hands or confronting suspects, warning that such actions could endanger lives and jeopardise investigations. The post New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NASA to Cover 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission Space Station Departure
item.description: A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft supporting the company’s 34th commercial resupply services mission for NASA departs the International Space Station following its undocking from the Harmony module’s forward port. Credit: NASA/Jessica Meir NASA and its international partners are set to receive scientific research samples and hardware as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft departs the International Space Station no earlier than Wednesday, Nov. 18, for its return to Earth. Pending weather conditions, the Dragon spacecraft will undock from the Harmony module’s space-facing port at 11:05 a.m. EST, following a command sent by ground controllers at SpaceX’s facility in Hawthorne, California. NASA’s live coverage of undocking and departure begins at 10:45 a.m., streaming through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online: https://www.nasa.gov/live NASA and SpaceX are monitoring weather forecasts and targeting splashdown off the California coast no earlier than 1:50 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 19 (10:50 p.m. PST Nov. 18). Teams will adjust plans as needed based on splashdown conditions in the Dragon recovery area and will provide updates on splashdown timing when available. NASA will not stream the splashdown but will post updates on its space station blog . Thousands of pounds of cargo are returning from the space station, including research samples that could advance future space exploration and improve life on Earth. The returning research includes a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct scientists used to study vascular aging and cardiovascular disease in space and on Earth. Frozen tumor organoids treated aboard the station also will return, helping researchers identify new ways to improve cancer treatments and advance personalized medicine. Scientists will analyze frozen microbial samples to better understand how antibiotic-resistant bacteria survive, adapt, and evolve in space. In addition, a lighting system will return after more than three years aboard the space station, where researchers tested its potential to support astronauts’ sleep and well-being during long-duration missions. Filled with more than 6,300 pounds of crew supplies, science investigations, and equipment, the spacecraft arrived at the space station on Oct. 15. It launched two days earlier on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida for the agency’s SpaceX 35th commercial resupply services mission. For more than 26 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs not possible on Earth. The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis and Moon Base programs, and to Mars. item.title: Ebonyi demolishes shop over planning violations
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has demolished a shop on Ejiofor Street, Abakaliki, over alleged failure to obtain building plan approval and encroachment on designated land. The demolition was carried out by the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning. Speaking during the exercise, the Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Richard Ugo Idike, said the property owner commenced construction without obtaining the required building plan approval from the ministry. Idike explained that building plan approval was mandatory to enable the ministry assess proposed structures, conduct necessary inspections and provide professional guidance to ensure compliance with physical planning standards. He said securing approval before commencing construction would also allow the ministry to identify potential structural, environmental and planning concerns and advise property owners accordingly. The commissioner cautioned property owners and developers against unauthorised construction and encroachment on designated lands, warning that the state government would enforce relevant planning regulations against defaulters. Idike was accompanied during the exercise by the Head of the Town Planning Department, TPL Esther Nwite, other town planners and members of the ministry’s task force. He urged residents, developers and property owners in Abakaliki to obtain the necessary building plan approval from the ministry before embarking on construction projects. The commissioner reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to enforcing physical planning regulations and promoting orderly development in the state capital. The post Ebonyi demolishes shop over planning violations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu transmits mental health amendment bill to Senate
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the National Mental Health Amendment Bill, 2026 to the Senate, seeking decriminalisation of attempted suicide and support for survivors. Senate ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌​‌‌‍​‌​President Godswill Akpabio, who announced the transmission during plenary on Tuesday, said that the proposed amendment would address concerns surrounding criminal penalties for attempted suicide. Akpabio said his earlier comments had excluded persons experiencing mental illness, whose condition could affect their ability to understand their actions when attempting suicide. “Perhaps, with this amendment, I should make a distinction in my earlier submission. “I had said that if someone attempts suicide, such a person should ensure that the attempt succeeds. Otherwise, the person would be sent to prison. “However, I did not include people who are mentally disturbed. I made that distinction because they do not have the mental balance to understand what they are doing. “I want to thank the president for supporting the decriminalisation of attempted suicide because making it a criminal offence for people who are mentally disturbed would be insensitive,” he said. Akpabio said the amendment was important, adding that the bill would decriminalise attempted suicide, particularly in cases involving people who were mentally disturbed. “When I made my earlier submission, I clearly stated that I was referring to people who were mentally sound, not those who were mentally disturbed. Unfortunately, social media reports did not capture that distinction. “Nevertheless, this is a welcome development. People who are mentally disturbed require our support,” he added. The senate president, thereafter, referred the bill to the Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action, urging its consideration as soon as practicable. item.title: Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05%
item.description: By Ozumba Chika Tony Elumelu, Chairman of Heirs Holdings, has increased his stake in Seplat Energy Plc to 22.05 per cent following the acquisition of additional shares valued at approximately $70 million. The latest purchase, made through Heirs Energies Limited, involved 5,888,341 ordinary shares, representing about one per cent of the company. The transaction was disclosed to the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday in a notification signed by Edith Onwuchekwa, Seplat Energy’s Director, Legal and Company Secretary. According to the disclosure, Heirs Energies Limited, a company controlled by Elumelu, acquired the shares from the company. Following the transaction, Heirs Energies’ direct shareholding in Seplat rose to 33,832,208 shares. The disclosure added that entities controlled by Elumelu — Heirs Energies Limited and Heirs Holdings Limited — now hold a combined 132,288,341 shares, representing a voting interest of 22.05 per cent of Seplat’s issued share capital of 599,944,561 shares. The company said the notification was made in compliance with Rule 17.15(c) of the NGX Rulebook 2015 on disclosure of dealings in issuers’ shares and Article 19(3) of the United Kingdom Market Abuse Regulations. The latest acquisition follows a similar transaction in September, when Elumelu, through Heirs Energies, purchased six million Seplat shares for £53.2 million. That transaction raised the combined shareholding of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings in the company to 21.07 per cent. Meanwhile, Seplat also disclosed a separate insider transaction involving its Chairman, Udoma Udo Udoma. The company said Tierce Investments Limited, a firm wholly owned by Udoma, purchased Seplat Energy’s 9.125 per cent Senior Unsecured Notes due March 21, 2030. The notes had a face value of $370,000, while the cash consideration for the purchase was $397,076.81. The post Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05% appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Passenger vows never to fly United Nigeria Airlines over early departure – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has said a passenger sent him a message last week threatening never to fly with the airline again because it departed earlier than its advertised time. Okonkwo said the passenger complained that while United Nigeria Airlines advertised an 11:30am departure, it took off at 11:20am. He spoke during a dialogue on Responsible Business Communication: Building Trust and Financing Investments for Sustainable Human Development at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, in Abuja, where he urged organisations to always tell the truth, saying it was the best reputation management strategy. He said: “A typical Nigerian traveller has his mind set on the timely departure of the airline, and if anything happens, you have to communicate the truth. You may have an AOG, technical issues, and sometimes that message doesn’t really sink. “I had a passenger last week who sent me a message saying they will never fly United Nigeria Airlines anymore and I said, why? He said, because they left on time. He said United Nigeria Airlines advertised departure for 11:30am but departed at 11:20am, and as the chairman, I was actually worried about how to respond. “I wanted to get angry, I wanted to shout back at him. But again, my experience being a member of this forum came into play, and I simply sent him a message saying, ‘I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.’ That was my answer. He never got back.” He also recounted an incident in which UNA diverted to Asaba instead of Abuja, saying the aircraft was scheduled to fly from Lagos to Abuja but landed in Asaba following an error by the dispatcher, who mistakenly entered Asaba as the destination in the flight documentation. He said the pilots followed the destination indicated in the documents and landed accordingly, while the cabin crew, believing they had arrived in Abuja, welcomed passengers to the Federal Capital Territory. According to him, the incident itself was not necessarily a major crisis until the airline’s communication team issued an inaccurate explanation. Okonkwo said the airline’s communication team, in an attempt to protect the company’s reputation, attributed the incident to bad weather in Abuja, despite the fact that the aircraft had landed in Asaba because of an error in its flight documentation. He, however, maintained that organisations must not confuse reputation protection with withholding or manipulating facts, warning that attempts to conceal the truth could eventually cause greater damage than the original crisis. He added that telling verified truths demonstrates respect for stakeholders and helps build confidence in an organisation, irrespective of how uncomfortable the information might be. He said: “The best word of public relations is to tell the truth and challenge responsibly. Whenever the truth is told, it builds trust, it builds confidence, and it also shows respect for stakeholder

item.title: Astronomers discover rare black holes that formed when stars failed to go supernova
item.description: null Gravitational waves have revealed a population of black holes that may have been born when masssive stars failed to go supernova. Most of us know the origin story of black holes , or we thought we did. Massive stars run out of the fuel for nuclear fusion and their cores collapse. As this happens, the stars' outer layers expand outwards. Shockwaves from the core collapse strike the outer layers, triggering a supernova explosion. The collapsed core creates a black hole. However, new research based on gravitational wave data collected by LIGO (Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory) and its gravitational wave detector partners, Virgo and KAGRA (Kamioka Gravitational Wave Detector), suggests this might not be the complete picture of black hole birth. The team behind the research suggests some massive stars go out with a whimper rather than a bang and that these "failed supernovas" can also spawn black holes. The hint of this comes from the over 300 black hole collisions spotted by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA since the detectors first "heard" ripples in space from these distant events in 2015. "A vast majority of the merging black holes in the universe are about 10 times the mass of our sun," LIGO team member Katerina Chatziioannou, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement. "Our data are showing that this group of black holes may have a common origin — they may be a distinct subpopulation that failed to go supernova. "These results represent a connection between the gravitational-wave data and underlying astrophysics we are trying to extract." Mass and spin of black holes indicate stars died with a whimper not a bang Currently, there is no hard evidence of failed supernovas, but their existence is well supported theoretically. In fact, scientists think there is a vast population of massive stars out there that imploded rather than exploded, directly collapsing into black holes. And these may be black holes with around ten times the mass of the sun (10 solar masses) found in merging pairs. Chatziioannou led a team that examined gravitational wave data to confirm this concept. To do this, they looked at the distribution of the masses of 257 black hole mergers detected by the LIGO – Virgo – KAGRA network over the past 10 years. This revealed a peak of 10-solar-mass black holes that represented 75% of the entire sample. If this was expected, what the team found that wasn't predicted was a lack of black holes with masses 12 to 16 times the mass of the sun. "We see 10 solar-mass black holes merging all the time," team member Isaac Legred of the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign said. "But why are, say, 14 solar-mass black holes so rare? The gap we see in the distribution of masses indicates there may be a special cocktail of internal physics that goes into forming the abundance of 10 solar-mass black holes." item.title: ULA lost a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying 40 Amazon satellites 10 minutes after launch — but the failure began just after liftoff
item.description: null The failure of a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying a full load of internet satellites for Amazon was caused by an anomaly in its first-stage booster, rocket maker United Launch Alliance said today (Nov. 17). That failure — which led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites — was recognized about 10 minutes after liftoff, but the problems began much earlier than that, ULA said in a statement. "While we appear to have lost telemetry and the mission at approximately 10 minutes into flight, early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance, resulting in stage separation occurring when the vehicle was low in altitude and below minimal velocity to reach orbit," ULA wrote in today's update . The two-stage Vulcan Centaur is the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket, which will retire after just six more flights. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and now has a total of five launches under its belt. The new rocket has experienced problems on three of those missions. On both its second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — the nozzle of one of Vulcan's strap-on solid rocket boosters (SRBs) fell off about 30 seconds after liftoff. On both occasions, the rocket overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payloads to orbit. However, after the second occurrence, the U.S. Space Force paused national-security launches with Vulcan until ULA addressed the SRB nozzle issue. (The February 2026 flight was a Space Force mission.) That work led to "design and process improvements to the nozzle," ULA said in an Oct. 28 update . And those tweaks apparently worked. "All indications are that the solid rocket booster performance was nominal, following nozzle improvements implemented for this launch," the company wrote in today's update. Vulcan's Centaur V upper stage, which features two RL-10C engines, did its job as well "but was unable to recover from the [booster] performance loss, resulting in loss of mission," ULA added. The Vulcan Centaur lifts off from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Vulcan's first-stage booster is powered by two BE-4 engines, which are built by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin . Today's update did not identify the exact problem with the booster; doing so will require more time, as the investigation has just begun. If that investigation finds a serious issue with the BE-4, there could be broad ripple effects across the American space program. After all, that engine also powers the first stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, which is a key piece of hardware for NASA's Artemis program of moon exploration. (And New Glenn is currently recovering from a failure of its own — a massive explosion on the test stand that occurred on May 28 .) NASA plans to integrate the Centaur V upper stage into its Space Launch System moon rocket, the vehicle that launches Artemis astronauts

item.title: Entertainment Week Africa officially kicks Off 5th Edition in Lagos | November 17th – 22nd
item.description: Entertainment Week Africa (EWA) , the pan-African platform for the business of creativity, opens its fifth edition in Lagos tomorrow, Wednesday, 18 November. The programme runs until Saturday, 21 November, and brings together creators, executives, investors, policymakers and delegations from more than 18 African countries. This year’s theme, Five Years of Closing the Gap, reflects the purpose EWA was built around: connecting African talent with the capital, markets, skills and audiences it needs to grow. Since its first edition, EWA has welcomed more than 67,800 attendees. The 2025 edition alone recorded 28,683 pass-holders from over eight countries and 50 industries, across 61 sessions, 93 film screenings, 20 music showcases and nine fashion showcases. By day and by night The week runs across two venues. By day, EbonyLife Place on Victoria Island hosts panels, roundtables, workshops, masterclasses, and film screenings. By night, the programme moves to the Livespot Entertarium in Ikate, beginning with Opening Night on 18 November at 6pm, an evening of music, fashion, film, comedy and awards. The Entertarium also houses the week’s experiences, including an exhibition, the EWA Art Floor, a fashion show, comedy, live music, a beauty exhibition and a marketplace. Seven tracks, one market The 2026 programme is organised across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Live Events & Production; Creative Enterprise; and Art & Animation, which is new this year. Alongside the conference, EWA runs a set of commercial formats designed to move deals forward. They include the EWA Deal Room, the Content and Music Markets, the EWA Capital Desk, the Creators Hub and LABSPOT, EWA’s skills and enterprise development engine. Last year’s Deal Room received more than 178 entries and advanced nine companies to its accelerator, with Future Africa, Catalyst Fund, Consonance Invest and Askya Investment Partners among the participating investors and partners. Between 30 and 40 per cent of this year’s delegates are expected to travel from outside Nigeria, with delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana, Senegal, Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa among them. The edition will also host the exclusive screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios, written by Dami Elebe , executive produced by Deola Art Alade. The road to Lagos The fifth edition follows a year in which EWA took its conversation abroad through EWA Creative Connect, its invitation-only convenings. The first was held in Los Angeles during Grammy Week, with executives from Warner Records, Adobe, Amazon and Unilever among the participants. The second took place in London during the Nigeria–UK state visit, with the British Film Institute, Diageo and the Ministry of Trade and Investment in attendance. The third, in Lagos on 12 November, was hosted by U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth. What The Founders Say “African creativity deserves stronger platforms,

item.title: America's hyperscale bit barns draw as much power as entire states
item.description: Just 403 hyperscale datacenters consumed an estimated 1.8 percent of US electricity in 2024-25, and their carbon dioxide emissions were roughly two to three times an earlier forecast for 2018. Research led by the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and the Harvard Data Science Initiative looked specifically at hyperscale facilities, the largest class of server farms that typically support cloud computing and AI processing. The published study, " Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres ," estimates their combined electricity use approached that of a single state such as Indiana, Michigan, or Tennessee under the highest-load scenario. The researchers identified 403 hyperscale facilities by using a larger datacenter dataset, satellite imagery, and building footprints on OpenStreetMap. Rather than reading electricity meters, the researchers worked out consumption from each site's electrical capacity, the hours in a year, and assumptions about how heavily the facility was running. Across four operating scenarios, ranging from low-intensity use to AI-heavy workloads, electricity draw was believed to total 68-99 terawatt-hours (TWh). Each of those states consumed approximately 100 TWh during the study period. The researchers also calculated carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions using eGRID2023 plant-level generation and emissions data from the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Emissions ranged from 21 million to 31 million metric tons of CO 2 across the scenarios, with a central estimate of 25.7 million. That compares with 10.5 million for 2018. The study covered May 2024 to April 2025, so electricity demand and carbon emissions are likely to be even higher now, the researchers say. "What we're seeing is already striking, but it's only a snapshot of a rapidly expanding industry," said Gianluca Guidi, lead author on the paper and postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard. "The datacenter boom hasn't slowed down since our study period ended in April 2025. New facilities have been built, existing campuses have expanded, and demand for AI computing continues to grow. That means the electricity use and carbon footprint we're reporting could already be substantially larger now in 2026." Harvard's report also considers the mix of fuels being used to generate the electricity that powers all those hyperscale data houses. The mix varies considerably between regional grids, so where a hyperscale facility is built makes a substantial difference to its attributed emissions. Across the sites studied, roughly 54 percent of the electricity attributed to their consumption came from fossil fuels, mainly natural gas and coal. The electricity attributed to these facilities nevertheless had a lower average carbon intensity than the US grid overall. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop from the lunar surface
item.description: null On Nov. 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft made the first liftoff from the lunar surface. Surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there. It took television pictures of the surface and learned about the composition of lunar soil. Then came the big liftoff. First Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away. Next, Surveyor 6 took pictures of its original landing site. Flight controllers on Earth could see the landing pad prints of Surveyor 6. They also saw an imprint from the rocket exhaust when Surveyor 6 lifted off. Surveyor 6 showed that spacecraft could land on the moon, and lift off again. Less than two years later, humans did the same thing during Apollo 11 . A panorama of the moon from NASA's Surveyor 6 moon lander in November 1967. (Image credit: NASA/GSFC/LROC) Why it mattered NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft launched to the moon on Nov. 7, 1967 and made its first landing on the lunar surface on Nov. 10 of that year. It's primary mission was to make a soft landing on the moon in the Sinus Medii of the moon. The probe took nearly 30,000 photos of the moon during its 16 days on the lunar surface, with the lander shutting down due to the onset of lunar night on Nov. 26. Surveyor 6 was the sixth and penultimate moon mission of NASA's Surveyor lunar program, so a lot of what it did (launching and landing on the moon ) had been done before. But a lunar liftoff? That was something new. This Boeing diagram depicts the short launch and hop on the moon by NASA's Surveyor 6 moon lander on Nov. 17, 1967. (Image credit: NASA/GSFC/LROC via Boeing) "On November 17, as an engineering test to see if its rockets could be restarted on the Moon, Surveyor’s engines fired for 2.5 seconds, lifting the spacecraft 12 feet high and moving it 8 feet west of its original landing site, in the first powered liftoff from another celestial body," NASA wrote in a mission overview . The engineering test proved that a spacecraft could land on the moon, and then lift off and take flight once more. That capability was a core requirement for NASA's Apollo astronaut moon landings that followed, since astronauts needed a way to return home after visiting the moon. But there was critical science Surveyor 6 was able to do with the lunar hop. "This maneuver provided excellent views of the surface disturbances produced by the initial landing and the effects of firing rocket engines close to the lunar surface," scientists with the Lunar and Planetary Institute wrote in a summary . "Photography obtained after the hop contributed to the soil mechanics investigation." Surveyor 6 also had a bar magnet on its footpad that allowed scientists to test how magnetic the lunar regolith was at the landing site. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: NICER Status Updates
item.description: November 17, 2026 NASA’s NICER Telescope Ends Science Operations After studying the universe for six and a half years beyond its initial mission, NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer) telescope on the International Space Station has ended science operations. The mission and space station teams are now focused on plans to finalize NICER’s 8-year archive of X-ray science observations and decommission and detach the telescope from its perch near the station’s starboard solar array. In June 2025, NICER was suddenly unable to swivel side-to-side beyond its current orientation, which limited its ability to track cosmic objects. The team paused data collection to investigate the issue. Robotic cameras on the outside of the station collected photographs of NICER that helped eliminate external causes. After an extensive investigation, engineers think an internal motor has failed, limiting the telescope’s motion. Launched in 2017, NICER embarked on an initial 18-month prime mission. Since then, it has made groundbreaking measurements of neutron stars , which contain the densest matter in the universe that we can measure, and revolutionized our understanding of black holes , active galaxies , and other mysterious phenomena in our universe. The telescope also successfully demonstrated the potential of pulsar-based spacecraft navigation in X-rays that could be used for travel to Mars and beyond. Closer to home, technology developed to test NICER before launch is being incorporated into prototype portable CT scanners , materials analysis systems, and other applications. August 5, 2025 Science Observations Remain Paused for NASA’s NICER Telescope Science operations by NASA’s NICER (Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer), an X-ray telescope on the International Space Station, remain paused as the team continues to evaluate the telescope’s systems after an issue developed with one of its motors. The motor is unable to move NICER beyond its current position side to side, and the telescope’s status has not changed since operations were halted June 17. The primary goal is to move NICER into its stowed configuration in case it needs to accommodate space station activities, though the current placement does not pose a safety issue to the station or crew. The team currently does not have a timeframe for returning to science operations. Photos taken by robotic cameras outside the station are helping eliminate external causes for the issue. Now the team is coordinating with space station personnel to perform troubleshooting maneuvers and determine potential causes within the payload. Since it began observing the X-ray universe in 2017, NICER has successfully demonstrated a form of deep space navigation that could be used for travel to Mars and beyond.
