item.title: Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Situational Awareness Dumps Bitcoin Miners After Citadel Sale Situational Awareness, the artificial intelligence hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, cut its bitcoin miner holdings sharply in the third quarter, leaving about $80.8 million across three stocks and exiting three others, a Monday filing shows. The San Francisco firm still held 3,019,029 CleanSpark shares, worth $38.9 million at Sept. 30, 1,934,618 Bitdeer shares, worth $20.3 million, and 527,864 IREN shares, worth $21.6 million. Those are the only miner lines left, a sliver of the $1.83 billion in six miner stocks the fund listed at June 30. IREN Cut 94%, and three miners are gone The deepest cut was IREN. The fund held 9,474,099 IREN shares, worth $433.3 million, at midyear. The Sept. 30 stake is about 94% smaller by share count. CleanSpark was trimmed about 75%, from 12,276,139 shares worth $178.6 million. Bitdeer was reduced about 44%, from 3,439,450 shares worth $54.6 million. Bitdeer’s reported value fell further than its share count, to $20.3 million, as the stock also declined. Three names disappeared from the filing entirely. The fund had held 26,008,473 Core Scientific shares, worth $665.6 million, 17,100,000 Riot Platforms shares, worth $468.2 million, and 9,133,726 Hive Digital shares, worth $33.2 million, at June 30. None of those lines appear in the new report. The filing does not say whether those sales were part of a late-July portfolio sale, later trades, or both. An AI thesis that ran through Bitcoin miners Aschenbrenner published a long 2024 essay, “Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead,” arguing that artificial general intelligence was approaching faster than most investors appreciated, and that computing power and electricity would be the tight constraints. He founded the fund that September around that view, looking at technology and energy companies that AI would help or hurt. The miner stakes fit the same idea. A March profile described the fund as betting that electricity and computing capacity may be the most valuable assets in the AI build-out, pointing to miners that were turning high-density facilities and power contracts toward AI workloads. IREN has signed a multiyear cloud contract with Microsoft. CleanSpark has struck a $6.6 billion data-center lease. Listed miners have also been operating under tight economics this year, with bitcoin often trading below estimated production costs. A July sale to Citadel, then a much smaller filing The cuts landed after a brutal July. The fund sold the bulk of the fund’s public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel late that month after heavy losses on AI-related holdings, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources said the fund was forced to unwind most of its public book. In a letter to investors, Aschenbrenner said the portfolio was down an estimated 67% in July, that the fund had come “closer to permanent capital impairment than is acce

item.title: OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents
item.description: California sued OpenAI yesterday, alleging it has tried to evade responsibility for the Hugging Face attack and about 80 other incidents in which the company lost control of its AI. The lawsuit was filed under the state's public nuisance and unfair competition laws. The July 2026 hack of Hugging Face and other attacks carried out by OpenAI's autonomous agents "may just be the tip of the iceberg," said a lawsuit filed in a state court by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. "OpenAI recently admitted to the Attorney General’s Office that it has lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing." OpenAI had publicly reported only 27 such incidents, showing that "OpenAI’s public reports do not represent the full scope of loss-of-control incidents involving OpenAI’s models that have impacted third parties," the lawsuit said. OpenAI "knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it," Bonta said in a press release . Read full article Comments

item.title: Inspiring FOSS project Crosspoint Reader has lessons about tech, communities, and LLMs
item.description: The Ubuntu Summit isn't all about Ubuntu, or even Linux. The second day opened with a talk from CrossPoint Reader project lead Justin Mitchell, with both good and bad news for all kinds of FOSS. The talk, EPUBs, ESP32s, and Everyone's A Developer Now , was all about a FOSS project that isn't Linux-based – because the devices it targets are much too small to run even the smallest, most cut-down distro. Recently, a new generation of roughly credit-card sized ebook readers has been thriving. Some have integral magnets, which let them cling to the back of iPhones – or to models with magnetically attached wireless chargers, anyway. The idea is that instead of waking your phone and doom-scrolling, you flip it over and read a book. They are bringing about what Mitchell calls "the Tiktok-ification of reading." Many of them, though, come from their various manufacturers significantly limited by their original OSes. The strong sales are linked to the availability of free, open-source, cross-platform alternative firmware, which removes many of the restrictions that the devices ship with. For most of them, that means Crosspoint Reader . Some devices are now shipping, new, with versions of Crosspoint Reader. This runs on multiple different models of compact e-readers, and this small community project has seen impressively widespread adoption: over 300,000 installations. Early in his talk, project lead Mitchell mentioned more than 1,600 forks on GitHub, but at the time of writing, that's up to 2,300 and counting. He estimates nearly half a million users. This kind of success forced Crosspoint Reader to change from being FOSS code to a product. A peripheral example is the Brick Club List , a list of what versions work with what devices – an Excel spreadsheet that grew into a website. If you haven't been paying attention, you may not have noticed just how much e-readers have shrunk – in size and in cost – in the last few years. The Reg FOSS desk first noticed this trend in 2024, when we read about the smartphone-sized Onyx Palma , which sold for around $300 (about £225). As it happens, this was a decade after The Register first looked at one of Boox's devices . Mini e-readers – and their prices – have continued shrinking since. The $99 (£75) Xteink X4 Classic has a 4.- inch (10.9 cm) screen, and the $79 (£59) Xteink X3 is even smaller: it's the size of a credit card, with a 3.7-inch (9.4 cm) screen. As a result of their strong sales, there are now multiple similar devices on sale, such as the Boox Picco . The project's GitHub page lists 11 devices it currently supports, all of which are based around the ESP32-C3 system on a chip. The ESP32-C series chips are more powerful than the earlier models of ESP32 microcontrollers: they have a single RISC-V core, but running in the low hundreds of MHz and with some 400 kB of RAM, of which about 380 kB is available. It's very little space, but enough to have fun. Mitchell talked about some of the problems of being a FOSS p

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I’ve never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. Continue reading...

item.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
item.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. Andrew Uaboi , Vice

item.title: SAP's cloud migration chief is migrating to Ionos as CEO
item.description: SAP chief customer officer Thomas Saueressig is leaving the German software giant to become CEO of hosting and cloud provider Ionos. The ERP and biz application vendor confirmed his departure on Tuesday, saying he will remain responsible for his current duties until the end of March 2027. He will succeed Ionos CEO Achim Weiß on April 1. In January, Saueressig will begin handing over responsibilities to Emmanuel Raptopoulos, currently a regional customer success president, who will take charge on an interim basis. SAP's supervisory board is searching for a permanent successor. Saueressig joined SAP's executive board in 2019 and became chief customer officer in April 2026. He leads the Customer Value Group and is charged with overseeing sales, customer success, services, and delivery, including adoption of SAP's cloud and AI products. In previous roles at SAP, Saueressig was responsible for customer services and delivery. He has also led product engineering, and has served as SAP's in-house CIO responsible for IT strategy and cloud transformation. He joined SAP in 2004 through its combined work-and-study program. His departure follows several changes at the top of SAP in recent years. In September 2024, CTO Jürgen Müller left by mutual agreement following an "incident" at a company event earlier in the year. In a statement, Müller said his behavior had been inappropriate. The company announced he would get paid €7.1 million following his departure. Chief revenue officer Scott Russell also left in 2024 by mutual agreement with the supervisory board. Julia White left the role of chief marketing and solutions officer in August 2024. "Thomas Saueressig has been a valued member of the Executive Board and has made significant contributions to SAP's transformation," said Pekka Ala-Pietilä, chair of SAP's supervisory board. "Over many years, he has helped sharpen SAP's focus on execution, customer value and operational excellence. We thank him for his commitment and wish him all the best for the future." Saueressig's departure comes as SAP pushes to move the ERP systems underpinning thousands of customers' businesses into the cloud – an effort whose operations and infrastructure he helped oversee. ®

item.title: NASA to Conduct Low-Altitude Flights Over Texas Farmland
item.description: Editor’s Note: This article was originally published on Oct. 15, 2026, and has been updated to correct the location and update the duration of the flight deployment. A NASA Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Amarillo, Texas, from Thursday, Oct. 22, through Monday, Nov. 2. These flights will measure gaseous and particulate emissions from animal feeding operations. A photo of the Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft, which will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Amarillo, Texas, to measure emissions in October and November 2026. Dynamic Aviation Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems. The FarmFlux mission will deploy more than a dozen sensors to measure ozone, methane, ammonia, particulates, and other pollutants rising from crop lands and livestock farms and their interaction with the Earth’s atmosphere. The mission is jointly led by NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland; Colorado State University; and Boston University. Additional low-altitude research flights with a NASA P-3 Orion aircraft are scheduled for the March to July 2027 growing season in the Midwest and California’s Central Valley with a focus on cropland. For more information about the FarmFlux mission, visit: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/evs-4/farm-flux/ By Sharon Teitelbaum NASA’s Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley

item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5072-5076: The Return of the Polygons
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 2 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5072-5076: The Return of the Polygons NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this image of a portion of the area in front of the rover, in which the return of the regular, well-expressed polygons captured several weeks ago can be seen. Curiosity used its Mast Camera (MastCam) to capture this image on Sol 5073, or Martian day 5,073 of the Mars Science Laboratory mission, at 15:45:05 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Abigail Fraeman, Deputy Project Scientist, Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology Earth planning date: Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 Curiosity’s past several weeks have been very focused on drilling and analysis of the “Basque Lakes” and “Nazca” samples. We learned a lot from those drilled samples, but it’s time to hit the Martian road again and resume our climb up Mount Sharp. The Yardang unit on the upper part of the mountain is calling! As we climb higher on Mount Sharp, we’ll continue to use many of our less resource intensive science instruments like APXS, ChemCam, MAHLI, and Mastcam to document the chemistry and textures of the rocks we encounter while making purposeful upward progress. These measurements allow us to document changes in the environments that formed the rocks and that altered them over time. The two areas we explored this week had rocks that were crisscrossed by lots of small, regular sized polygons surrounded by raised ridges. This texture was very similar to the rocks we encountered a few months ago slightly lower on the mountain . Those unique textures really surprised us when we first saw them, and we’ve been spending time as a science team discussing how they may have formed. Polygonal textures like these can form under a variety of different conditions including shrinkage of the surface when water is lost from minerals, temperature cycling, or compaction and expansion after being buried and exposed. The data Curiosity collected this week give us more clues about the genesis of these features and what they reveal about the evolution of Mars’ habitability. We’ll also get information about the composition of the cements that form the raised ridges around the polygons. In the orbital view of our future route, I can see the layers that we’ll reach next week or the week after have textures very similar to where we first saw the amazing field of polygons. So I’m guessing we’ll continue to encounter polygons in the next couple drives, and that they’ll look more dramatic and expansive with each drive. But this is just a guess! item.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to View Roman Telescope’s First Images
item.description: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, seen here in the clean room at the agency’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, on Nov. 25, 2025, will explore essential questions in the areas of dark energy, exoplanets, and astrophysics. Credit: NASA/Jolearra Tshiteya NASA will release the first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope during a live stream from the American Geophysical Union (AGU) Annual Meeting in San Francisco at 3:30 p.m. EST (12:30 p.m. PST) Monday, Dec. 7. The images will showcase the unique scientific capabilities of Roman, which will soon capture deep, panoramic, never-before-seen views of the universe to explore the mysteries of dark energy, dark matter, and worlds outside our solar system. Watch the unveiling on a variety of platforms online: https://www.nasa.gov/live Roman’s first images will simultaneously post on the agency’s website . The following is a list of activities for release of the first images (all times Eastern): Dec. 7 12 p.m.: NASA will preview the images for media under embargo as part of the AGU meeting in San Francisco. To participate, either remotely or in-person, media must be registered with AGU by 8 p.m. Sunday, Dec. 6. Media can apply for AGU registration online . NASA will update this advisory later with briefing participants. The agency also will offer embargoed interviews following the conclusion of the briefing to registered media. A recording of the media briefing will be available on the AGU website after the embargo lifts at 3:30 p.m. on Dec. 7. 2:45 p.m.: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will participate in a fireside chat at the AGU meeting, moderated by journalist Alex Witze, to discuss the powerful connections between Earth and space science, the discoveries shaping our understanding of the universe, and the role NASA science plays in advancing what is possible. 3:30 p.m.: The live broadcast for the release of Roman’s images will stream through a variety of NASA platforms, in addition to AGU channels. Tuesday, Dec. 8 6 a.m. – 1 p.m.: Roman mission experts available to conduct live, remote interviews with broadcast media. More details about scheduling these interviews are forthcoming. Pixel adoption NASA invites the public to claim a corner of the universe with one of Roman’s select first images . When Roman reveals its first images, each pixel will represent a unique piece of the cosmos. Once the image is revealed, participants can look up their personal pixel and receive a digital trading card with key information they can share with NASA social accounts. Roman community events Get involved by hosting your own event for the reveal of Roman’s first images. Roman launched Aug. 30 from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, beginning a three-month, million-mile trip to its final orbit at the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2. item.title: Opting out of Gemini tracking? Google will still hold your data 20x longer
item.description: Opting out of Gemini chat retention is about to mean a lot less thanks to a quietly announced Google update. Google on Monday said that it was making changes to Gemini chat history that, at first glance, makes it seem like users are simply getting more control over their discussions with the Chocolate Factory’s chatbot. At the core of the announcement is Google's splitting of Gemini chat history settings from AI model training permissions. What that means is that users will now be able to store their chat histories with Gemini without also having to opt in to allow their conversations to be used to train those same models, as was previously the case. So far so good: Being able to have Gemini remember more of your past interactions to contextualize newer discussions is nice, to be sure. The second part of the announcement, however, might raise one's privacy hackles. "Now, if you turn your new History setting off, future chats will be saved for around two months," Google notes. "They're used to respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public." Google said it is making that change in the name of making Gemini safer and more secure, but it fails to mention that the chat retention period for users who turned their history off had been just 72 hours before this update. That's right: Prior to Monday's change, Gemini users who turned off the "Keep Activity" option only had their chats retained for three days, according to an archived copy of the same page that now states that choosing the same please-don't-store-my-AI-chats option means Google keeps them "for around two months." It's also worth noting that, even if users have the option to not store Gemini chat records enabled, submitting a feedback request on any Gemini post means that temporary retention period gets extended to three years. That was the case both before and after Monday's change, mind you, but for the privacy-conscious it's definitely important to note. Sending feedback to Google about a Gemini response also means that humans will be reviewing that particular conversation, as well as any associated files and conversations that can be associated with the one in question. Submitting feedback also means that Google assumes the right to use the conversation and its associated content to improve its services and improve its AI models. In other words, even if you opt out of having your conversations stored, your Gemini history could still end up being used to feed the Google machine. The company didn't respond to questions for this story. ®

item.title: NASA wants you to 'shine bright' today for Voyager 1's light-day milestone. Here's how
item.description: null As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft. The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth . And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency. To celebrate the spacecraft, participants can use a flashlight, phone, bike light or other portable light source to send the signal skyward. And don't fret if you're unfamiliar with Morse code : NASA has created an automated flasher that can be opened in a smartphone or tablet browser to display the VGR sequence. The spacecraft’s call sign pattern consists of three quick flashes followed by one long flash for the letter V, two long flashes and one quick flash for G, and one quick flash, one long flash and another quick flash for R. Participants are encouraged to repeat the sequence for about a minute, NASA officials said. The three-letter call sign for NASA's Voyager mission, VGR, spelled out in Morse code. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) NASA also invites people to photograph or record their light signals and share them on social media, tagging the agency's official account, @NASA. The goal is to create a worldwide display of light marking a milestone nearly five decades in the making. The celebration is intended as a symbolic tribute rather than an actual attempt to communicate with Voyager 1 . At a distance of one light-day from Earth, the spacecraft is so far away that even radio signals traveling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach it. A flashlight or phone signal from Earth, of course, cannot reach the probe; NASA communicates with it using its Deep Space Network of radio dishes. Voyager 1 will get one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) Launched on Sept. 5, 1977, Voyager 1 has spent nearly 50 years traveling through space and is now the most distant human-made object from Earth. When it reaches the one-light-day milestone, it will have traveled a distance that light itself takes 24 hours to cross. Its twin, Voyager 2 , is expected to reach the same milestone in November 2035. (The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system.) The public celebration will be followed by another opportunity to learn more about the historic mission. item.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
item.description: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road. As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity. Read full article Comments

item.title: Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Launches ChatGPT Plugin for Trading Bitcoin, Stocks, and Derivatives Coinbase launched an official plugin for ChatGPT on Tuesday that lets users connect a Coinbase account and trade bitcoin, other cryptocurrencies, stocks and derivatives without leaving the conversation, provided they approve every order. The company said the tool puts trading “in the same chat you use for everything else.” Users can connect an account, review a portfolio and place orders from ChatGPT on the web, on mobile or on desktop. Chief executive Brian Armstrong wrote that “starting today anyone with ChatGPT can connect their Coinbase account” and can “trade right inside your Coinbase account.” Coinbase posted a link to the official plugin in ChatGPT’s directory. Its developer documentation describes a short setup: sign in, review the access being requested and choose which portfolios the plugin can see. Interactive confirmation cards in the chat cover new orders, edits, cancellations and conversions between dollars and USDC. Read-only requests, such as checking a balance, do not use them. Bitcoin, Stocks and Dated Futures, With a Card on Every Trade The announcement did not single out bitcoin, but the plugin sits on the same rails as Coinbase for Agents, the company’s toolkit for connecting AI apps to a trading account. That documentation lists spot trading in more than 900 pairs, including bitcoin, along with eligible U.S. stocks and dated futures from Coinbase Financial Markets. The examples include a market buy of bitcoin and a dated bitcoin futures contract. Orders go through Advanced Trade, so those fees and eligibility rules apply. Fees vary by product, fee tier and whether an order adds or takes liquidity, and they are shown on the order preview. The official plugin is narrower than the full agent toolkit. A separate custom connection is required for the company’s Global Derivatives products and for x402 payments, which agents can use to buy market data. Coinbase already offers U.S. customers stock and ETF trading on its own platform, but the agent documentation says equity orders trade during regular market hours by default. The plugin should not be read as a new around-the-clock stock venue. What a user can buy still depends on the products already attached to that account. Official Access Is Limited to U.S. Coinbase Users Armstrong’s “anyone with ChatGPT” line is broader than the documentation. The official plugin is currently available to U.S. Coinbase users, and availability also depends on a user’s ChatGPT account and workspace. If the plugin does not appear, the company tells users to check their workspace’s plugin policy. In a disclaimer attached to Tuesday’s announcement, it said product availability, eligibility and Coinbase entities “vary by jurisdiction,” that trading can result in a total loss, and that “AI agents may fail.” The same post said users direct all AI activity and assume full responsibility. item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. item.title: Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Trezor Shipping Partner Breach Exposes 27,000 Orders as Customers Report Scam Calls Trezor said Monday that a data breach at Skladon, one of its shipping partners, exposed personal information tied to about 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, and that some customers have already reported scam calls. The company’s own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved. Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15 of unauthorized access to systems that held customer shipping data. The breach itself took place on Nov. 7. Trezor believes the attacker exported records for orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7. An investigation is ongoing. Names, addresses and purchase details were leaked The exposed records included full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses, order dates, and the products purchased and their prices. Trezor said neither it nor Skladon ever holds wallet backups, PINs or passphrases, so the breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer’s bitcoin. It does give a stranger a home address and proof that the person bought a device designed to store crypto. Anyone who received Trezor’s incident email and ordered in that window was affected. A small number of customers who ordered between Aug. 9 and 14 may also be included, but the company cannot email them because those details had already been anonymized under its 90-day retention policy. It is reaching those buyers through its blog and posted the same warning on X. Skladon does not ship to the United States, Trezor said, so U.S. customers were not affected by this incident. The company added that Skladon delivers to many countries, and that the leak is not limited to one region. Trezor warns of scam calls Trezor told customers to treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about their order as suspicious, and to be alert to potential risks to their physical security. Scammers may quote real order details, including what was bought and what was paid, to make a message look genuine. Some customers have already reported scam calls. “Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup,” the company said . Customers should contact support only through the company’s website, never through a link, QR code or number in an unsolicited message, and should never enter a wallet backup anywhere except on their device. If a message contains a threat or makes someone feel unsafe, Trezor said to contact local police first. The third partner incident this year This is not the first time a Trezor contractor has lost customer data. In August, a breach at shipping provider ShipMonk exposed records from 13,689 customers, including 11,742 with full names, emails, phone numbers and shipping addresses. Trezor later said another approximately 67,000 U.S. customers who ordered between November 2019 and August 2021 were also affected, after ShipMonk failed to delete records it had assured the company were gone. item.title: Hackers smash 'n' grab AI vendor: Take off with license data of Uber drivers
item.description: Uber has confirmed that nearly 150,000 people had their personal information compromised after hackers broke into one of its AI suppliers. A filing with Oregon's attorney general puts the number of victims at 149,346. Among the data the crooks got their hands on were images of drivers' licenses and information extracted from them, including names, home addresses, dates of birth, and license numbers. Uber doesn't name the supplier in its filings with US state attorneys general, but told TechCrunch it was Fireworks AI, the inference outfit whose security woes we covered last week . According to a breach notification filed with Iowa's attorney general, Fireworks alerted Uber to the intrusion on October 9. Uber cut off the supplier's access to its data and, four days later, established that the attackers had accessed drivers' personal information on October 7. Uber had set up a dedicated cloud storage environment for the AI biz, complete with security monitoring overseen by its own cloud security team. Unfortunately for Uber and its drivers, the crooks were using legitimate credentials, so none of the alarms went off. The ride-hailing firm says those credentials couldn't be used to access its other systems, and says it has since revoked or changed the credentials associated with the supplier. Uber hasn't said why it handed images of thousands of driver's licenses to an AI inference outfit. The Register has put that question to both companies, and asked Uber if any drivers outside the US had their data exposed. Fireworks, which provides infrastructure for developers to run and fine-tune AI models, had a particularly miserable October. The company first disclosed a security incident on October 9 after discovering that someone had been using its internal credentials without permission. Fireworks initially said it had no evidence that the intruders had gotten their hands on personal information or customer datasets. The company was hacked again later that month and, on November 9, disclosed that some customer data had indeed been compromised. The AI biz acknowledged that attackers had accessed billing records, some customer datasets, and incomplete model weights. Productivity software maker Notion was among those affected, with some of its customers' conversations with its AI assistant exposed. Fireworks suspects the involvement of financially motivated criminals in the business of flogging unauthorized access to large language models. Whether the crooks have any plans for the haul of Uber drivers' personal information is unclear. Uber began notifying affected individuals on November 10, more than a month after learning of the breach. It's offering victims free credit monitoring and fraud assistance, though drivers have just 90 days from the date of their letter to sign up. This isn't Uber's first brush with cybercriminals in recent months. In August, the ride-hailing giant's logistics arm, Uber Freight, confirmed a break-in after the Helix extortion cre

item.title: Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Wells Fargo More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Stake to $2.35 Billion Wells Fargo more than doubled its holdings of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust in the third quarter to 49.6 million shares worth $2.35 billion at Sept. 30, though bitcoin’s slide since then has cut the stake’s value to about $1.82 billion. The bank disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Monday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It reported 49,577,094 IBIT shares across five of its units, up from 24,396,222 shares worth $812.2 million in its filing for June 30. That is an increase of about 103% in share count. The reported value rose about 189%, because IBIT climbed from $33.29 to $47.34 a share during the quarter. The fund closed at $36.79 on Monday. At that price, the same 49.6 million shares are worth roughly $1.82 billion, about $520 million less than the value in the filing. JUST IN: Wells Fargo disclosed 49.6 million shares of BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin ETF currently worth $1.82 billion, making them the largest institutional BTC ETF holder. That’s an ~200% increase from 24.4 million shares in Q2! pic.twitter.com/1GpMFeB8Ow — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 16, 2026 Mostly client accounts, not a house bet The filing does not break out how much of the position belongs to the bank and how much to its customers. But the largest single block, 32,483,714 shares worth about $1.54 billion, sits under Wells Fargo Clearing Services, the brokerage entity behind Wells Fargo Advisors. Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network reported another 9.5 million shares, and Wells Fargo Bank reported 7.4 million. That points to a position built largely by wealth-management clients buying the ETF in brokerage and advisory accounts, rather than a directional trade by the bank itself. A 13F lists securities over which a firm has investment discretion, which at a big bank includes managed client money. Wells Fargo Securities, the investment-banking and trading arm, also reported IBIT options: calls on 717,200 shares and puts on 540,000 shares, valued at about $34.0 million and $25.6 million. Those figures reflect the value of the underlying shares, not the premiums paid, and they may hedge other positions. Both lines were smaller than at midyear, when the unit listed calls on 1.12 million shares and puts on 845,000. Wells Fargo also added to its other spot bitcoin funds. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust rose to 3.09 million shares, worth $114.1 million, from 2.56 million. Bitwise’s bitcoin ETF rose to 1.6 million shares, worth $72.6 million, from 1.38 million. Strategy stake cut by a third The bank moved the other way on Strategy (MSTR). Wells Fargo’s long position in the bitcoin treasury company fell to 1,339,018 shares, worth $205.0 million at Sept. 30, from 1,994,253 shares at midyear, a drop of about 33%. item.title: Windows 11 previews remote padlock only IT can open
item.description: A new experimental Windows 11 build previews security features including an Intune-controlled Remote Lock, while a beta build clears away another relic from the halcyon days of Windows Phone. The security changes include viewing and individually removing passkeys stored on FIDO2 (Fast Identity Online 2) security keys, plus a preview of the Microsoft Pluton Cryptographic Provider. For enterprise administrators, though, Remote Lock is the main attraction. Finding a lost Windows device has been around for years, and you can also remotely wipe a device to prevent data from falling into the wrong hands. Remote Lock lets an administrator lock a managed device through Intune without wiping it. The instruction takes effect at the device's next check-in. Windows signs out of every active session, hides every sign-in option, and shows a locked screen. The lock survives restarts and the device going offline – only an administrator can lift it remotely. Microsoft's documentation spells out the restriction: "There is no offline or local unlock. No PIN, password, local admin, or web sign-in works on a locked device; unlock arrives only through Intune." Once the lock is applied, even stolen credentials won't restore access through the normal sign-in screen. The user's account itself is not affected; this applies only to the specific device. Though still in preview, the feature will allow IT teams to respond non-destructively to a report of a missing device. It doesn't erase data or isolate the device from the network (Microsoft directs admins to other Intune controls if that is required). The lock doesn't block Safe Mode, Windows Recovery Environment, or booting from external media. Microsoft advises keeping BitLocker enabled to protect the data. Now for the beta build, where Microsoft, in time-honored fashion, gives and takes away. The latest Windows Insider build hammers another nail into the coffin of Microsoft Maps. The Maps app was removed from the Microsoft Store and made nonfunctional in July 2025. Now Offline Maps settings are following it out, as Microsoft retires the Windows UWP Map control and Windows Maps platform APIs. The original Maps app dates back to Windows Phone 7 and appeared on the desktop with Windows 8. It continued through subsequent versions before Microsoft stopped preinstalling it with Windows 11 version 24H2. For those with a nostalgic streak, it's another piece of Windows Phone disappearing off the map. ®

item.title: Goldman Sachs More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Holdings to $1.28 Billion
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Goldman Sachs More Than Doubles Its Bitcoin ETF Holdings to $1.28 Billion Goldman Sachs more than doubled its spot bitcoin ETF holdings in the third quarter to about $1.28 billion, driven by a 52-fold jump in Fidelity’s fund, while cutting its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than half, a Monday filing shows. The bank reported the positions in a Form 13F covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. Its long holdings across five spot bitcoin funds were valued at $1.283 billion, up from about $580 million in its filing for June 30, an increase of roughly 121%. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust remained Goldman’s largest bitcoin fund holding, at 16,440,599 shares worth $778.3 million. The share count actually slipped about 5% from 17,232,201 at midyear. The value rose because IBIT climbed from $33.29 to $47.34 a share during the quarter, a gain of about 42%. The bigger change was in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund. Goldman held 5,477,583 FBTC shares worth $397.9 million at Sept. 30, up from just 105,840 shares, worth $5.4 million, three months earlier. A new stake in Morgan Stanley’s bitcoin fund Goldman also reported 2,000,020 shares of the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust, worth $47.9 million. The fund, ticker MSBT, launched in April as the first bitcoin product from a U.S. bank-affiliated asset manager, with a 0.14% sponsor fee. Goldman’s June filing did not list it. The trust reported 36.42 million shares outstanding and $873.4 million in net assets at Sept. 30, so Goldman held about 5.5% of the fund. The rest of the bitcoin fund book was smaller. Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust rose to 1,383,498 shares, worth $51.1 million, from 22,905. Goldman also listed 120,600 shares of the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust, worth $7.8 million, alongside puts on the same number of shares, which suggests that position is hedged. The bank’s options book in IBIT is large, too. It reported puts on 7,513,000 IBIT shares, valued at $355.7 million, and calls on 4,895,600 shares, valued at $231.8 million. Those figures reflect the value of the underlying shares, not premiums paid, so they do not measure money at risk. Goldman runs one of Wall Street’s biggest market-making and derivatives businesses, and its 13F does not say which positions are hedges for clients and which are its own views. Strategy shares cut, Strategy puts held The bank went the other way on Strategy. Goldman’s long position in the bitcoin treasury company fell to 2,760,766 shares, worth $422.6 million at Sept. 30, from 5,810,162 shares at midyear, a drop of about 52%. Its Strategy put options barely moved, covering 4,738,700 shares worth $725.4 million, compared with 4,735,800 in June. Calls rose to 707,200 shares from 575,900. Strategy closed at $103.03 on Monday, down from $153.09 at the end of September, as the company keeps buying bitcoin and buying back preferred stock. The pattern mirrors the one at Wells Fargo, whose own 13F, also filed Monday, showed its IBIT stake more than doubling wh

item.title: Bitcoin Policy Institute Renames to Finney Foundation for Open Technology
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Policy Institute Renames to Finney Foundation for Open Technology The Bitcoin Policy Institute announced Tuesday that it is now the Finney Foundation for Open Technology, a new parent organization whose brief spans open-source artificial intelligence, digital cash and encrypted messaging. The institute’s bitcoin work continues inside the foundation, and bitcoin remains a primary focus. The name honors Hal Finney (1956-2014), a cryptographer and software developer who helped build the email encryption program PGP, ran one of the first anonymous remailers and received the first bitcoin transaction from Satoshi Nakamoto in January 2009. In a November 1992 essay, Finney wrote that the computer “can be used as a tool to liberate and protect people, rather than to control them.” He was diagnosed with ALS the same year he received that first transaction and died in 2014. The Foundation’s case for open systems Washington is now writing the rules for artificial intelligence, the foundation said, and fear drives much of that debate. As the Bitcoin Policy Institute did for bitcoin, the Finney Foundation said it will argue that open systems outcompete closed ones, that individuals should control the tools they rely on, and that American strength comes from building in the open. “We set out to make Washington think about Bitcoin differently — to educate them on the importance of open monetary networks,” said David Zell, president of the Finney Foundation. “Our fellows now serve in congressional offices for both parties and in the executive branch. Our ideas have shaped discourse and policy. Our expansion will help us stay at the forefront of today’s most consequential policy debates, especially those around open source AI.” That argument was already on stage in September at Freedom Tech DC, the institute’s Washington summit, formerly the Bitcoin Policy Summit. The invite-only gathering put open-source and open-weight AI, data centers and energy infrastructure on the agenda alongside bitcoin and dollar-backed stablecoins. Block co-founder Jack Dorsey said there that “the next and probably largest element [of freedom technology] is open intelligence and making sure that it’s not locked up in the hands of any one government or any one company… that’s where we’re going to get the best outcomes.” A declaration and a new class of fellows Alongside the new name, the foundation published an Open Technology Declaration, titled “For Us, Not Over Us,” which argues for machines that serve people rather than rule over them. The text takes up Finney’s line about computers as tools of liberation and says the foundation will offer research, policy ideas and educational programs aimed at that goal. It asks who the new machines are for and who is in control of them, and it calls for people to build the tools they need without waiting for permission. It is also launching an inaugural class of Finney Fellows, researchers with expertise spanning machine i

item.title: Twenty One Capital (XXI) Buys 154 Bitcoin, Its First Purchase of 2026
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Twenty One Capital (XXI) Buys 154 Bitcoin, Its First Purchase of 2026 Twenty One Capital bought 154.32 bitcoin for about $10 million in cash after the weekend selloff, the company said Monday, its first disclosed purchase of 2026 and a small addition to a treasury that had barely moved all year. The Tether-controlled company said it paid an average of about $64,801 per coin, bringing its holdings to about 43,668 BTC as of Nov. 16. At Tuesday morning’s price near $64,900, that stack is worth roughly $2.83 billion. “Bitcoin is our benchmark for every investment decision we make. Any business we acquire has to beat simply buying more Bitcoin, and this weekend’s drop in price made adding Bitcoin an easy decision,” CEO Rapha Zagury said in the release. “Every dollar we spend, whether on Bitcoin, acquisitions, or buybacks, is weighed against maintaining flexibility to run our business well,” he added. A treasury that sat still for nine months The buy breaks a long pause. Twenty One’s quarterly report , filed Nov. 13, shows it held 43,515 BTC at the end of 2025 and 43,514 BTC on Sept. 30. The only change in between was a single bitcoin transferred on March 31 as a vendor payment. The same filing shows how much room the company has to keep buying with cash. Twenty One reported $102.8 million in cash and equivalents at Sept. 30, down from $117.7 million at the end of 2025. The $10 million purchase equals about a tenth of that September balance, although the company has not said how much cash it holds now. Twenty One also carries $486.5 million of convertible notes issued when it went public. Those notes are secured by about 16,116 BTC pledged as collateral, coins the filing says are not available for general corporate purposes while they back the debt. The company’s bitcoin cost basis was about $3.69 billion at Sept. 30, or roughly $84,900 per coin. The new coins came in about $20,000 below that average, but the treasury as a whole remains underwater at current prices. Shares trade below bitcoin Twenty One’s Class A shares closed at $4.56 on Monday, down 7.9% on the day, before the purchase was announced after the market close. The 10-Q lists 346.65 million Class A shares outstanding, which at that price are worth about $1.58 billion, well below the market value of the company’s bitcoin. That gap has been the central problem for Zagury since he replaced founder Jack Mallers as CEO in July. In an August shareholder letter, he acknowledged investor concerns about the stock trading at a discount to its bitcoin and said Twenty One “must become more than a Bitcoin treasury.” Tether took control of the company in May after buying out SoftBank’s stake. The company’s latest shareholder letter, released Nov. 13 with third-quarter results, laid out a plan to build cash-generating businesses around the bitcoin treasury. Twenty One reported third-quarter net income of $1.087 billion, almost all of it from a $1.093 billion gain in the fair value of it

item.title: Russia Lets Everyday Investors Buy Bitcoin Starting Today
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia Lets Everyday Investors Buy Bitcoin Starting Today Everyday investors in Russia can legally buy bitcoin through regulated brokers and crypto exchange offices starting Tuesday, but two of the country’s biggest retail brokers, T-Bank and VTB, are not offering it yet. The Bank of Russia ordinance that took effect Nov. 17 approves bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, the legal term for ordinary retail buyers who do not meet Russia’s wealth or experience thresholds. From the same date, exchanges may admit those three assets to public trading. Retail buyers can purchase through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary are capped at 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the central bank’s official rate on Tuesday. The cap applies per intermediary, not per person. Qualified investors face no cap and can access any crypto asset. Every buyer, regardless of status, must pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before the first trade. JUST IN: Starting today, Russian retail investors can now legally buy Bitcoin pic.twitter.com/EzifKUtcea — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 17, 2026 T-Bank and VTB are still testing The legal door opened before the apps did. “The main reason T-Bank clients do not yet see cryptocurrencies in their banking app is the absence of a market standard for testing,” Alexander Kretov, head of blockchain technology development at T-Bank, told TASS on Tuesday. “As soon as the Bank of Russia publishes it on its official website, we are ready to launch external operations.” Kretov said T-Bank’s crypto exchange office and digital depository are built and in the final stages of live testing, and that the service will roll out in several stages, “starting with the most active users.” VTB’s brokerage arm told the agency it is testing the customer journey in its VTB My Investments app and is waiting for the remaining regulations. Once those land, it plans to open crypto trading first to qualified investors who pass the test. The central bank added VTB to its registries of digital depositories and crypto exchangers in October, and the broker ran its first crypto trades for corporate clients the same month. The single test that brokers are waiting on has been drafted by two industry groups, NEXUS and NAUFOR. As of Nov. 10, the draft had been sent to the Bank of Russia for approval as part of a basic investor-protection standard, but it had not been approved. NAUFOR won self-regulatory status for crypto exchanges and digital depositories in October. Exchange trading comes next in Russia Tuesday’s rule is the first of several dates on Russia’s calendar. A separate central bank ordinance lets exchanges open organized crypto trading from Nov. 22, once the regulator has approved their trading rules. item.title: Nvidia places chip exports under boardroom supervision after Huang's exit
item.description: Nvidia's board has created a national security and export control committee amid intense scrutiny over co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang's departure and allegations that Singapore-based customer Megaspeed diverted GPUs to China. The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee , announced on Tuesday, will monitor Nvidia's national security policies, export compliance, and global trade risks. It will meet at least quarterly. The committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. Nvidia's existing National Security and Global Trade Compliance teams will report on day-to-day operations directly to this new committee, as well as to interim CEO Colette Kress. The panel will oversee efforts to strengthen Nvidia's national security and trade compliance teams and retain independent legal, national security, and trade experts. The announcement follows the resignation of Huang last week after he admitted to an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, and was allegedly involved in a second relationship with an Nvidia employee. US authorities reportedly suspected Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, an allegation that has not been proven. Megaspeed has separately faced scrutiny over suspected export control violations. The US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice confirmed on Tuesday in a joint statement that they were investigating Megaspeed back in 2024. The agencies said they would pursue any criminal conduct uncovered by the investigation. However, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs stated that US authorities had provided only "limited assistance" when they were investigating the activities of Alice Huang and Megaspeed, as The Register reported. The New York Times also reported that US investigations into Megaspeed were halted last year after an Nvidia executive contacted Commerce Department officials. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has issued new regulations tightening up restrictions on AI technology exports and cloud operators offering remote access to it. The US also expanded its Pax Silica initiative , getting allied nations to sign an agreement that "guarding AI supply chains" is a shared responsibility. Nvidia says it recognizes that advanced silicon and AI technologies present challenges for national security, and it has a responsibility to address them. "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," said Harvey Jones, chair of Nvidia's board of directors. ®

item.title: ISS astronauts 3D print human cells and tissues | Space photo of the day for Nov. 17, 2026
item.description: null NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins works in the Life Sciences Glovebox on the ISS. (Image credit: Jessica Watkins/NASA) Astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station . Recently, NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins got to work supporting an ongoing experiment that includes 3D-printing human cells and tissues in space. What is it? Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research. Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media. In the image she is gloved-up with both her hands and arms covered in the sealed glovebox while she mixes samples of living cells with a bioink, a mixture she then inserts into a specialized cartridge, NASA shared . Why is it incredible? This experiment that Watkins is working on "leverages the microgravity environment of ISS to 3D print cells and manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Just one of many examples of how we’re using this amazing orbital national laboratory to reshape our understanding of biology, medicine, and engineering, and improve life on Earth!" Watkins shared online . This experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth. When you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments. On the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

item.title: Website owners thumb their noses at EU privacy rules, researcher finds
item.description: Privacy? What privacy? The 100 most-visited English-language sites are flouting European data protection laws on a massive scale, according to a privacy researcher's investigation. Forensic data analysis , published by Alexander Hanff, an attorney, computer scientist, and occasional contributor to The Register , with the support of SOMI (Stichting Onderzoek Marktinformatie), a Netherlands-based privacy group, details the dubious data flow. From October 1 to 3, 2026, Hanff took a clean Google Chrome browser profile and measured what happens when the browser loads the 100 most visited English-language websites for five minutes, without any consent banner interaction. At these 100 sites, visits were made to 265 pages – the home page, the privacy page, and the cookie notice when available – which resulted in 518,770 privacy events without any consent. All 100 sites produced what the report characterizes as Tier 1 events – interception, exfiltration, or high-entropy fingerprinting (a total of 14,675). Tier 2 consists of storage on the device, capturing device characteristics, and script loads without consent (284,463 events recorded). Tier 3 includes protocol mechanisms and passive reads used for tracking (219,632 events). The median website triggered 2,695 events, for a total of 28,695 events deemed high or critical. And 92.4 percent of the servers contacted during this process were on networks outside the European Economic Area (EEA). Most of these servers – 1,247 out of 1,400 – were in the US, and 1,034 belonged to third-parties. The EU General Data Protection Regulation governs the transfer of personal data outside the EEA. The EU allows data transfers to the US for organizations participating in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Beyond that, according to Hanff and SOMI, a valid legal mechanism like a contract must be in place or the transfer may fail to meet GDPR or the ePrivacy Directive. In some cases, California Penal Code section 631 (interception) and section 502 (computer access) may also be relevant. On these 100 websites, there were 89,437 fingerprinting events, 1,492 cookies set without consent, 7,456 scripts loaded from other origins, 18 websites implementing CNAME cloaking, and 37 websites delivering code to use the browser's built-in AI interfaces. The privacy and cookie notices on these websites imposed a median reading time requirement of 28 minutes and none fully matched what their pages did. Among the sites' consent banners, 115 out of 165 used dark patterns, like steering visitors with emotional language about a "safer" or "better" experience, or "we care about your privacy." The report, released in conjunction with a presentation at the Field Talk conference , also calculates the estimated environmental impact to load all this third-party content on websites without consent: 1,271,444 kWh per year, or enough to power 353 homes in Europe at 3.6 MWh per home annually. item.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
item.description: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge. It’s “worse than a bug” Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Optimizely hack turns world's biggest websites into malware dispensers
item.description: Some of the world's most popular websites spent Monday serving malware to visitors after crooks found a way into a piece of software used to A/B test web pages. Scott Helme, a security researcher at Report URI, identified malicious JavaScript being served by websites belonging to at least 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, IKEA, Salesforce, HSB, and TalkTalk. All have one thing in common: they use Optimizely's Web Experimentation software. Optimizely allows businesses to tweak the content and layout of their websites without changing the underlying site code. Unfortunately, someone other than its paying customers figured out how to do just that. The attackers abused a feature that allows Optimizely customers to add their own JavaScript to web pages. The malicious code was distributed alongside the legitimate stuff from Optimizely's own content delivery network, giving customers little reason to suspect anything was amiss. Optimizely has since confirmed that the criminals exploited a vulnerability, dubbed "OPTIMJACK" by researchers, in the sign-up process for its experimentation software, adding that it had patched the hole, removed the offending code, revoked tokens, and notified affected customers. "Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects,” the company said. “We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered." Of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts examined by Helme and his team, 188 contained malicious code, including those used by Optimizely's own website and login portal. Given the researchers examined only a subset of the scripts, the number of affected businesses could be higher. The malware underwent several revisions over the course of Monday, with cryptocurrency theft among the crooks' money-making schemes. Copy a wallet address to your clipboard and the malware could quietly swap it out for one belonging to the attackers, diverting any funds sent to that address. A card skimmer added later in the day grabbed card numbers, expiration dates, and security codes from payment forms. However, according to a separate analysis by StepSecurity , card details entered into an iframe hosted by a third-party payment processor were beyond the malware's reach. There was something nasty in store for Apple users, too. The malware attempted to deploy the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits on iPhones and iPads running older versions of iOS, though how many devices the criminals managed to compromise is anyone's guess. Helme traced roughly $7,000 in cryptocurrency to the attackers' wallets on Monday, though there’s no telling how much more the crooks stand to make from stolen payment card details. item.title: 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966
item.description: null Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories. 'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life' "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights. "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound. "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust. "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever." A bright Leonid fireball captured during the meteor storm of 1966 above Wrightwood, California. (Image credit: NASA via Getty Images) 'Students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors, to watch' "I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time. "The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch. "We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and l

item.title: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI’s environmental footprint
item.description: The COP31 presidency hopes countries will commit to reducing the environmental impact of AI UN Climate Change/Kiara Worth Only nine countries have signed an international pledge to make AI greener, despite warnings at the COP31 climate summit that the technology’s growing energy demands threaten climate goals. The Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge was launched on 16 November at the summit in Turkey. Developed by the summit’s presidency and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), it intends to make AI more sustainable by encouraging cleaner energy use, more efficient data centres and greater transparency about the technology’s environmental footprint. Read more The secret weapon that could finally force climate action “AI and other frontier technologies are a double-edged sword,” said Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of UN Climate Change, at a press conference on 16 November. “The task ahead is to blunt their dangerous edges, sharpen their catalytic ones and put these technologies responsibly to work.” Advertisement But Ketan Joshi, an independent analyst researching AI’s climate impacts, questions that analogy. He says it conflates traditional machine learning, already used in applications such as weather forecasting, with energy-intensive generative AI. “You don’t need to have a giant, energy-hungry generative AI chatbot if you want to have better wind forecasting for a wind power developer,” he says. The initiative comes as AI’s rapid expansion is placing growing pressure on electricity grids. According to the International Energy Agency, electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres increased by 50 per cent in 2025. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Joshi says there is little evidence that technology companies are building enough renewable energy capacity to meet this growing demand. Even companies that have invested heavily in renewables, such as Amazon and Google, are increasingly turning to fossil fuels to support their rapid expansion, he says. The only countries to have endorsed the pledge so far are Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Luxembourg, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Korea, Turkey and Uganda. The pledge is voluntary, with no binding targets for cutting emissions or reducing energy consumption. It sets out four areas for action, including increasing the use of low- and zero-emission energy to power AI infrastructure, improving energy and water efficiency, and measuring the environmental impacts of AI systems. It also calls for greater financial and technical support to help developing countries use AI to tackle climate change. However, the agreement leaves considerable room for interpretation. The call for using “low- and zero-emission energy”, for example, allows continued reliance on fossil gas rather than committing to renewable electricity. item.title: 'Not rocket surgery' claims researcher who found six Danfoss fridge controller zero-days in under an hour
item.description: A Dutch cybersecurity researcher claims he found six zero-days in Danfoss refrigeration controller firmware in under an hour, then delivered a withering assessment of the vendor's defenses against memory corruption. The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) warns that the flaws could let attackers take control without credentials, potentially retain access after resets, or disable controllers altogether. Carlo Meijer of cyber consultancy Midnight Blue examined the latest AK-SM800A firmware, version 5.3.2, manually – no AI required. He said that he went looking in random places where strcpy() is invoked, given the vendor's "extremely liberal use" of the function (which doesn't check whether the destination buffer is large enough), and swiftly found five cases in which he said he could trigger a segfault with a one-line cURL command. "Of course, remotely triggering a crash is bad in itself, but being able to leverage the buffer overflow to obtain remote code execution is much worse," he wrote . Meijer added: "Any reasonably experienced exploit developer will agree exploiting straightforward stack-based buffer overflows on ARM Linux without exploit mitigations is very straightforward. And if they don't, there's probably a frontier or open-weight model out there willing to help them agree." He noted that before achieving RCE, an attacker would need to overcome the limitation of strcpy() where it stops copying bytes after hitting a null byte, but said "it's not exactly rocket surgery." He went on to claim: "Also, the exploited application runs as root (because of course it does)." Later firmware adds "session control," an authentication mechanism whose strict setting blocks unauthenticated access to most web interfaces. But Meijer found a memory corruption flaw in that protective layer too. He described the final zero-day as a "trivial" pre-auth memory corruption bug which again starts with a segfault but can be wangled into an RCE "with some additional effort." Meijer also considered whether attackers could maintain access after a reset, as seen with implants such as Saltwater and Firestarter . He considered this feasible because the controllers do not use their processor's secure boot features. "In such a scenario, an attacker could either retain remote access or leave a time-triggered payload for a 2nd (or 3rd...) strike – increasing damage by spoiling new batches of food," said Meijer. "Alternatively, attackers could simply wipe flash memory and/or push a malformed firmware update to brick the controllers and render them permanently inoperable – requiring costly and time-consuming replacement similar to the TTPs deployed during the December 2025 attack on the Polish electric grid ." Meijer's priority for operators was to remove the controllers' direct internet exposure, rather than spend scarce resources on piecemeal patching.
